name: Kanembu
world_status: statement found in an open source
sweep_summary: Kanembu is not in the catalog. All five titled items are about Kanembu prosody/accent. The only one read is Dybo (Russian original 1995 of the 1994 English translation; inslav.ru PDF already on file, scanned re-verified against the page images): Kanembu has a dynamic accent placed by a contour rule on the first high-toned syllable (first syllable in all-low words), i.e. tone-conditioned prominence on a two-tone system, matching the catalog's treatment of Central Kanuri; Dybo 2000 p. 6 restates it in one line. The four Jouannet works on Ngaldoukou Kanembu (1977 thesis, 1979 article, 1981 accentuation paper, 1982 SELAF book) are the first-hand descriptions and none is open: the 1982 book is HathiTrust search-only (UVA copy; MPI EVA shelf), the 1981 SELAF chapter is print-only, the 1977 thesis and 1979 Niamey article have no online trace. Acquisition priority: Jouannet 1982 and 1981 high, 1979/1977 medium.org, HathiTrust catalog, HAL, theses.fr and Crossref APIs only; all fetches and queries are ledgered in

new_statements.quote: Анализ акцентованных материалов по языкам и диалектам группы канури (диалект бáдави, диалект мáнга, кайди-канембу, канембу Нгури) показывает, что, по крайней мере, в части диалектов и языков этой группы существует силовой акцент, регулируемый тем же контурным правилом, что и в тубу (p. 270) … [в тубу] акцент падает на начало первой последовательности морфем (соответственно, слогов) высшей валентности, иначе говоря, на первый слог с высоким тоном (соответственно, с восходящим или нисходящим тоном, которые приравниваются в контурном правиле к высокому) (p. 269) … в последовательности, состоящей исключительно из низких тонов, акцент падает на первый слог (p. 271)
new_statements.translation: Analysis of the accent-marked materials for the languages and dialects of the Kanuri group (the Badawi dialect, the Manga dialect, Kaidi-Kanembu, Nguri Kanembu) shows that, at least in part of the dialects and languages of this group, there is a dynamic (force) accent regulated by the same contour rule as in Tubu (p. 270) … [in Tubu] the accent falls on the beginning of the first sequence of morphemes (respectively, syllables) of the highest valency, in other words on the first syllable with high tone (respectively, with rising or falling tone, which the contour rule treats as high) (p. 269) … in a sequence consisting exclusively of low tones, the accent falls on the first syllable (p. 271).
new_statements.citation: Дыбо, В. А. [Dybo, Vladimir A.]. 1995. Акцентуационные процессы в языках группы теда-канури и проблема происхождения парадигматических акцентных систем [Accentuation processes in the languages of the Teda-Kanuri group and the problem of the origin of paradigmatic accent systems]. Московский лингвистический журнал 1: 236–279.
new_statements.locator: pp. 269 (Tubu contour rule), 270 (Kanuri-group incl. Kaidi-Kanembu and Nguri Kanembu), 271 (all-low-tone words); footnotes 23–24 cite Lukas 1931 and Lukas 1959 as the Kanembu data
new_statements.reading: tone language with a stress statement
new_statements.second_reader_evidence: Opened (23 two-page spreads, no text layer) and re-rendered spreads 18-19 (MLJ pp. 268-271) at 150 dpi to read the page images directly, not the scanned. All three quoted passages are verbatim on the page: p. 269 (right half of spread 18): "...акцент в тубу регулируется контурным правилом балто-славянского типа, т.е. акцент падает на начало первой последовательности морфем (соответственно, слогов) высшей валентности, иначе говоря, на первый слог с высоким тоном (соответственно, с восходящим или нисходящим тоном, которые приравниваются в контурном правиле к высокому)."; p. 270 (left half of spread 19), first paragraph: "Анализ акцентованных материалов по языкам и диалектам группы канури (диа…
new_statements.rule_in_words: Kanembu has lexical/grammatical tone (H, L, and contour 'broken' tones from contraction) plus a dynamic word accent that is predictable from tone: it falls on the first high-toned syllable of the word form (rising/falling tones count as high); if the word has only low tones, it falls on the first syllable. Dybo 2000: I, p. 6 restates it as 'in Tubu, Kanuri (at least Badawi), Kanembu the stress is placed on the first high-toned syllable'.
new_statements.exceptions: Rare all-low accented forms arise where a final high tone is lowered before a closely bound following word (Dybo citing Lukas 1931 p. 64 n. 11, p. 76 n. 107); 1sg Indefinit I forms with low-toned roots (dauní, fanní, gullí) are said not to be exceptions; in Nguri Kanembu the verb accent is drifting toward a paradigmatic (lexical-class) accent (pp. 272–273).
new_statements.domain_note: Word forms (phonetic word) in Lukas's accent-marked vocabulary, grammar and texts; not an instrumental study. The statement is Dybo's comparative reanalysis of Lukas 1931 (Kaidi-Kanembu, one informant) and Lukas 1959 (Nguri), not first-hand fieldwork.
new_statements.identity_note: The rule is stated for Kaidi-Kanembu (Lukas 1931; Kanem, one Bornu-origin informant recorded in Cairo) and Nguri Kanembu (Lukas 1959; Glottolog dialect ngur1265) within kane1243, alongside Badawi and Manga Kanuri (kanu1279 group). Jouannet's Ngaldoukou (South Kanem) variety is not covered by the opened statement. Old Kanembu (tarj1235) material from Bondarev is a separate languoid.

new_statements.quote: Анализ акцентованных материалов по языкам и диалектам группы канури (диалект бадави, диалект манга, кайди-канембу, канембу Нгури) показывает, что, по крайней мере, в части диалектов и языков этой группы существует силовой акцент, регулируемый тем же контурным правилом, что и в тубу [...] Рассмотрение материала текстов кайди-канембу показывает, что это же правило прилагается и к сплошь низкотональной последовательности (т.е. в последовательности, состоящей исключительно из низких тонов, акцент падает на первый слог).
new_statements.translation: Analysis of the accent-marked materials on the languages and dialects of the Kanuri group (the Badawi dialect, the Manga dialect, Kaidi-Kanembu, Nguri Kanembu) shows that, at least in part of the dialects and languages of this group, there is a dynamic accent regulated by the same contour rule as in Tubu [i.e. p. 269: the accent falls on the first high-toned syllable, rising/falling tones counting as high] [...] Examination of the Kaidi-Kanembu texts shows that the same rule also applies to an entirely low-toned sequence (i.e. in a sequence consisting exclusively of low tones the accent falls on the first syllable).
new_statements.citation: Дыбо, В. А. 1995. Акцентуационные процессы в языках группы теда-канури и проблема происхождения парадигматических акцентных систем. Московский лингвистический журнал 1: 236-279 (Russian original of Dybo 1994, St. Petersburg Journal of African Studies 2: 29-50; 3: 27-44)
new_statements.locator: pp. 270-271 (rule defined p. 269; Kaidi-Kanembu word lists pp. 270-271 from Lukas 1931; Nguri Kanembu p. 272 from Lukas 1959)
new_statements.reading: Kanembu (Kaidi and Nguri dialects, Lukas 1931/1959 data as analysed by Dybo) is a two-tone language with a predictable dynamic accent placed on the first high-toned (or contour-toned) syllable of the word, defaulting to the first syllable in all-low words. Stress is therefore tone-conditioned, not fixed-position or weight-based; the language would be classed with its sister Central Kanuri (catalog: TONAL-OR-PITCH-ACCENT). Caveat: Dybo is reinterpreting Lukas's marked data, not reporting his own field observation; the first-hand descriptions are Jouannet 1977/1979/1981/1982 (unread, print-only).
